article.title: Trump lifts fuel economy restrictions on automakers
article.summary: ALBAWABA - The U.S. Department of Transportation has finalized a Trump resolution to loosen fuel economy and emission standards.The DoT described the move as “among the largest deregulatory actions under the second Trump Administration.”The move by the Trump administration finishes off the last of Biden-era restrictions on emissions and fuel economy; in Biden’s era, standards required fleet average fuel economy to reach 4.6 liters per 100km by model year 2031.President Trump’s plan requires 6.7 liters per 100km, not much higher than the 7.8 liters per 100km target previously set for model year 2024.Trump’s administration says this would have $1,300 off the average cost of a new vehicle, saving $138 billion over the next five years — though those figures have been disputed.The decision naturally pleases automakers to the detriment of consumer advocacy, health, and environmental groups who argue that easing the restrictions will make Americans pay more at the pump, along with increase...

article.summary: This is Heatmap Daily, a weekday news digest written by our executive editor.President Trump’s big fuel efficiency rollback is here. This afternoon, the Department of Transportation significantly weakened the Corporate Average Fuel Economy standards, the federal government’s rules that encourage new cars and trucks to get gradually more fuel-efficient over time. Instead of mandating that new cars and trucks hit a target of more than 50 miles per gallon, as the old Biden-era rules had required, new vehicles sold in the U.S. will now need to average only 34.9 miles per gallon.That target is below the level that most automakers havealreadyachieved in their vehicle fleet.
